argument_summary: The admissible record supports a narrower position than clean certification. Aggregate readiness passed and no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, which supports launch readiness overall. The same record also shows a real current weakness in the aviation maintenance triage slice. Under the policy, that does not require blocking certification if the current release packet is framed as caveated compliance and the weakness is treated as a disclosed material limitation for the named launch use case rather than as resolved. The overbroad claim to reject is that prior approval or informal monitoring already satisfies the requirement; the defensible claim is that certification is supportable only on a disclose-the-limitation basis.
claims_about_business_cost: No claim is made that business cost overrides policy. The narrower policy-consistent treatment avoids unnecessary escalation if the auditor accepts certification only in caveated form, with the subgroup weakness carried forward explicitly as a current disclosed limitation.
claims_about_policy: Policy does not permit treating the issue as resolved on the basis of stale approval or informal monitoring. It does permit certification to proceed only if current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and the material segment weakness is disclosed, unless there is an approved mitigation or risk acceptance. On the present evidence, the compliant framing is caveated compliance tied to disclosure of the current limitation, not clean compliance and not a finding that prior approval cures the current documentation gap.
concessions: The current record does not support any claim that the documentation requirement has already been fully satisfied for this release.
The current record does not include approved mitigation, risk acceptance, or owner sign-off for the aviation maintenance triage regression.
Prior approval from three months ago is context for model-family continuity, not a substitute for current-release evidence.
Informal post-launch monitoring is not an approved replacement for required disclosure or reviewed risk acceptance.
